name: the Parque de María Luisa
title: Ancient Trees in the Parque de María Luisa: 10 to Find
meta_description: Seville's second tallest tree, its widest plane and its tallest deciduous conifer all stand in this one park, measured by the city itself. Ten to find.
intro:
Three of the biggest trees Seville has ever measured stand in this one park. The city's 2022 survey of its singular trees puts a Norfolk Island pine near the Torre Norte at 44 metres, second tallest in Seville; a bald cypress over the duck island at 35.7 metres, the tallest deciduous conifer it found anywhere; and a plane on the Avenida de Bécquer at 4.70 metres round, the widest of its kind in the catalogue.

Ten of the trees we map are here, spread across a park of glorietas and artificial hills where finding them takes an afternoon rather than a lap. One of them came first and the monument came later: the bald cypress at the centre of the Glorieta de Bécquer was already growing when the city built a marble monument to the poet around it in 1911. Entry is free.
